questions.question: Kintsugi: Beauty in the Broken. Discuss. END OF THE QUESTION PAPER ***
questions.solution_html:
• Kintsugi: Beauty in the Broken. Discuss.
  • Ans: Instruction: A good response should demonstrate Understanding of the concept of Kintsugi
  • demonstrate a clear grasp of the underlying philosophies of Kintsugi, with accurate and insightful
  • discussion -- in error-Free construction (grammatically correct, and appropriate for the context).
  • Content: Japanese art of repairing pottery with gold -- Finding beauty in imperfection -- wabi-sabi
  • Acceptance of transience and imperfection -- Historical Background --Transition from functional repair
  • to artistic enhancement -- Kintsugi as a metaphor for resilience and personal growth --Emphasises
  • authenticity and embracing flaws --accept imperfections rather than conceal them -- Counteracting
  • societal obsession with perfection -- Promoting gratitude, mindfulness, and self-acceptance--Kintsugi is
  • more than art, a life philosophy --Inspires resilience, self-worth, and transformation of adversity into
  • opportunity -- Encourages recognition of beauty in the mended and imperfect. (1 × 15 = 15)
questions.final_answer: opportunity -- Encourages recognition of beauty in the mended and imperfect.

questions.question: What is Bierce suggesting about the future of humans and machines in terms of / vocabulary such as “autonomy” and “control”?
questions.solution_html:
• Bierce uses words like “autonomy” and “control” to suggest a future in which the
  • relationship between humans and machines becomes ambiguous and even threatening.
  • He warns that as machines grow more “autonomous,” humans risk surrendering their
  • control, possibly becoming secondary to the technology they created.
